proposals.evidence: Brokskat tīto bitter fits tikta through the attested Middle Indo-Aryan titta type. The separately recorded retroflex ʦ̣iṭo is excluded because Turner distinguishes its tṛṣṭa family.

proposals.primaryEvidenceText: 5806 tiktá 'pungent, bitter' MBh., tiktaka- R. [√tij] Pa. Pk. titta- 'pungent, acrid, bitter', Ku. tīto (whence titīṇo 'to be offended'), gng. tit, N. tito; A. titā 'bitter' (whence titikā 'slightly bitter'), B. tita, titā, Mth. tit, Bhoj. tī˜t; H. tītā 'pungent' (whence tittāl, °ār 'sharp, astute, knavish'); Si. tit 'pungent, bitter'; — P. tit 'bitter' perh. with ṭ for t to avoid tītā 'cunnus' rather than < tr̥ṣṭá-. — Tor. tid, f. tīd 'bitter' Grierson Tor 180 perh. mistake for *ṭiḍ < tr̥ṣṭá- in Sh.gil. c̣ĭṭŭ 'bitter'. *taiktikā-; *tiktapūra-; *rājikātiktaka-.

assignments.Notes: Brokskat tīto bitter fits tikta through the attested Middle Indo-Aryan titta type. The separately recorded retroflex ʦ̣iṭo is excluded because Turner distinguishes its tṛṣṭa family.

proposals.withdrawalReason: Withdrawn proposal 66 had linked tīto directly to tikta (5806), but Schmidt–Kaul p. 247 explicitly classifies this Brokskat word as a Kashmiri loan. The available Kashmiri ṭyoṭhᵘ bitter belongs to CDIAL 5938 tṛṣṭa and differs in vowel and consonants; the article’s Kashmiri table has no main-dialect bitter response, and its Kishtawari record is merged with hot. An exact donor correspondence must be checked before replacing the withdrawn direct-reflex assignment.
